tip: 마다 (mada = every) follows a noun: 해마다 (haemada = every year).
-고 싶다 = 'want to': 받고 싶어요 (batgo sipeoyo = want to receive).
-아서/어서 links cause and result: 받아서 기뻐요 (badaseo gippeoyo = got it, so glad).
Feelings about someone else normally take -어해요: 기뻐해요 (gippeohaeyo = is glad), not 기뻐요.
한테 (hante) marks the receiver: 후배들한테 (hubaedeulhante = to the juniors).
에 (e) marks a time: 저녁에 (jeonyeoge = in the evening).
가입하다 (gaipada = to join) takes 에: 동아리에 가입해요 (dongarie gaipaeyo).
(으)로 marks a role: 교환 학생으로 (gyohwan haksaengeuro = as an exchange student).
유학을 가요 (yuhageul gayo): 유학 (yuhak = study abroad) takes the object marker 을 (eul), even though the verb is 가다 (gada = go).
필요하다 (piryohada = to need) takes 이/가: 점수가 필요해요 (jeomsuga piryohaeyo).
-아/어지다 = 'become': 익숙해졌어요 (iksukaejeosseoyo = got used to).
For elders, use honorific -세요: 친절하세요 (chinjeolhaseyo = is kind).
-(으)ㄹ 거예요 = 'will': 갈 거예요 (gal geoyeyo = will go).
(으)로 marks the means: 점수로 (jeomsuro = by the score).
하나도 + 못 = 'not a single one': 하나도 못 풀었어요 (hanado mot pureosseoyo).
-고 = 'and then': 끝나고 (kkeunnago = it ends, and then).
때문에 (ttaemune = because of) follows a noun: 수능 때문에 (suneung ttaemune).
에 marks the destination: 학원에 보내요 (hagwone bonaeyo = send to the academy).
보다 (boda = than) marks comparison: 생각보다 (saenggakboda = than I thought).
The verb for taking an exam is 보다 (boda), literally 'to see': 시험을 봤어요 (siheomeul bwasseoyo = took the exam).
For someone you respect, the helping verb is 드리다 (deurida = give): 보여 드렸어요 (boyeo deuryeosseoyo = showed, humbly).
시험에 붙었어요 (siheome buteosseoyo) – note the 에 (e): you stick to the exam, so passing takes the 'to' particle, not an object marker.
합격할게요 (hapgyeokalgeyo) ends in -(으)ㄹ게요, a promise to your listener; plain -(으)ㄹ 거예요 would just predict, not commit.
Honorific past -셨어요: 발표하셨어요 (balpyohasyeosseoyo = announced).
신청하다 (sincheonghada = to apply) takes 을/를: 시험을 신청해요 (siheomeul sincheonghaeyo).
까지 (kkaji = until) marks a limit: 내일까지 (naeilkkaji = until tomorrow).
-(으)ㄹ 때 = 'when': 발표할 때 (balpyohal ttae = when presenting).
-씩 (-ssik) means 'each/apiece': 열 개씩 (yeol gaessik = ten each).
께 marks the honored receiver: 선생님께 (seonsaengnimkke = to the teacher).
만큼 (mankeum = as much as) follows a word: 노력한 만큼 (noryeokan mankeum = as much as you try).
